'''Wolf Reik''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of London|FRS]]<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/people/wolf-reik/ |title=Wolf Reik's FRS|website=royalsociety.org |year=2010|author=Anon|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London |access-date=2014-01-02}}</ref> is a German-British [[molecular biologist]] and an honorary group leader at the [[Babraham Institute]], honorary professor of [[Epigenetics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] and associate faculty at the [[Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.babraham.ac.uk/our-research/epigenetics/reik/|title=Wolf Reik's group|publisher= [[Babraham Institute]]|website=babraham.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sanger.ac.uk/research/faculty/wreik/|title=Wolf Reik at the Sanger|publisher=[[Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute]]|website=sanger.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> He was announced as the director of Altos Labs Cambridge Institute when the company launched on 19 January 2022.<ref>{{Cite press release |last=Labs |first=Altos |title=Altos Labs launches with the goal to transform medicine through cellular rejuvenation programming |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/altos-labs-launches-with-the-goal-to-transform-medicine-through-cellular-rejuvenation-programming-301463541.html |access-date=2022-04-08 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref>
==Early life and education==
Reik is the first child of four of Rosemarie Reik (nee Heiles) and Helmut Gottlieb Reik (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Reik) who were both physicists. Reik was born in Aachen on 22nd August 1957, attended primary school in Braunschweig, and secondary school in Freiburg. Reik studied Physics and Medicine at the University of Freiburg and completed his medical degree at the University of Hamburg. He obtained his MD in the lab of [[Rudolf Jaenisch]] and did postdoctoral work in the lab of [[Azim Surani]].

==Career and research==
Wolf Reik studies how additional information can be added to the [[genome]] through a range of processes collectively called [[epigenetics]]. He discovered some of the key epigenetic mechanisms important for mammalian development, physiology, genome reprogramming, and human diseases. His early work led to the discovery that the molecular mechanism of [[genomic imprinting]] is based on [[DNA methylation]].<ref name="Reik1987">Reik W, Collick A, Norris ML, Barton SC, Surani MA (1987) Genomic imprinting determines methylation of parental alleles in transgenic mice. ''Nature'' '''328''', 248-251</ref> He uncovered [[non-coding RNA]]<ref name="Smits2008">Smits G, Mungall AJ, Griffiths-Jones S, Smith P, Beury D, Matthews L, Rogers J, Pask AJ, Shaw G, VandeBerg JL, McCarrey JR, Renfree MB, Reik W, DunhamI (2008) Conservation of the H19 noncoding RNA and H19-IGF2 imprinting mechanism in therians. ''Nature Genetics'' '''40''', 971-976</ref> and [[chromatin]] looping<ref name="Murrell2004">Murrell A, Heeson S, Reik W (2004) Interaction between differentially methylated regions partitions the imprinted genes Igf2 and H19 into parent-specific chromatin loops. ''Nature genetics'' '''36''', 889-893</ref> regulating imprinted genes, which he showed to be involved in fetal nutrition, growth, and disease.<ref name="Constancia2002">{{cite journal|last1=Constância|first1=Miguel|last2=Hemberger|first2=Myriam|last3=Hughes|first3=Jennifer|last4=Dean|first4=Wendy|last5=Ferguson-Smith|first5=Anne|author-link5=Anne Ferguson-Smith|last6=Fundele|first6=Reinald|last7=Stewart|first7=Francesca|last8=Kelsey|first8=Gavin|last9=Fowden|first9=Abigail|last10=Sibley|first10=Colin|last11=Reik|first11=Wolf|author-link11=Wolf Reik|title=Placental-specific IGF-II is a major modulator of placental and fetal growth|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=417|issue=6892|year=2002|pages=945–948|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/nature00819|pmid= 12087403|s2cid=4421165 }} {{subscription required}}</ref> He found that the environment influences epigenetic programming in embryos, with changes in gene expression persisting in adults and their offspring.With his collaborators he discovered global epigenetic reprogramming in early embryos and in primordial germ cells10. He found that adult human cells could be substantially rejuvenated by epigenetic reprogramming induced by transient treatment with Yamanaka reprogramming factors11.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dean |first1=Wendy |title=Conservation of methylation reprogramming in mammalian development: aberrant reprogramming in cloned embryos |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=2001 |volume=98 |issue=24 |pages=13734–13738 |doi=10.1073/pnas.241522698|doi-access=free |pmid=11717434 |pmc=61110 |bibcode=2001PNAS...9813734D }}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gill |first1=Diljeet |title=Multi-omic rejuvenation of human cells by maturation phase transient reprogramming |journal=eLife |date=April 2022 |volume=11 |doi=10.7554/eLife.71624|doi-access=free |pmid=35390271 |pmc=9023058 }}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Wolf Reik has received many awards, including:

* 2011, elected member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Reik_Wolf |title=Wolf Reik's page at Academia Europaea |publisher=Ae-info.org |date= |access-date=2014-01-02}}</ref>
* 2010, elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name=frs/>
* 2003, elected to [[EMBO Membership]] at the [[European Molecular Biology Organisation]]{{citation needed|date=May 2017}}
* 2003 Elected [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FMedSci)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Wolf Reik |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Wolf-Reik-0033z00002qIIZzAAO |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref>
* 1994 awarded the Wellcome Prize in Physiology
